subject: Quarterly ops prep: capacity scenarios & unit-cost tradeoffs
messages:
From: Karthik Iyer <karthik_iyer@redwood.ai>
To: Marcus Lin <marcus_lin@redwood.ai>, Evelyn Hart <evelyn_hart@redwood.ai>, Laura Bennett <laura_bennett@redwood.ai>
Cc: Vivek Kulkarni <vivek_kulkarni@redwood.ai>
Date: Mon, 19 Oct 2026 09:02:00 -0700
Subject: Quarterly ops prep: capacity scenarios & unit-cost tradeoffs

Team —

We need a short, decision-grade packet for the upcoming leadership prep meeting (QBR prep slot on Oct 23). Specifically the execs want: a tight set of capacity scenarios for the next 12 months (baseline, growth+, and stress), the expected GPU spend for each, utilization targets to hit our unit-cost goals, and the sensitivity to batching and prefix/KV caching improvements.

Ask: Marcus, can you assemble three scenarios in the attached spreadsheet format with expected peak concurrent capacity (GPUs), average utilization, and monthly cost lines? Evelyn, can you overlay model mix, quantization assumptions, and expected token throughput so we can convert to $/1M tokens? Laura, please include ops risks & any lead times for adding Dedicated pools. I want a concise exec summary (1 page) and a 2-slide appendix with the key charts.

Constraints to assume: 10% month-over-month user growth in growth+, 2% in baseline. Include a stress scenario with a 30% sudden spike for one month. Highlight where batching/caching moves the needle vs. pure capacity increases.

Attachments: capacity_scenarios_v2.xlsx (spreadsheet) — template for numbers; unit_econ_assumptions.txt — baseline cost inputs.

Thanks — please send first pass by EOD Tue so I can synthesize before Wed leadership sync.

--
Karthik Iyer
Head of Infrastructure Planning
Redwood Inference
From: Marcus Lin <marcus_lin@redwood.ai>
To: Karthik Iyer <karthik_iyer@redwood.ai>, Evelyn Hart <evelyn_hart@redwood.ai>
Cc: Laura Bennett <laura_bennett@redwood.ai>, Vivek Kulkarni <vivek_kulkarni@redwood.ai>
Date: Mon, 19 Oct 2026 12:18:00 -0700
Subject: Re: Quarterly ops prep: capacity scenarios & unit-cost tradeoffs

Karthik —

Uploading first-pass numbers to the sheet (tab names: baseline / growth_plus / stress). High-level notes here:

- Baseline: assume current committed Dedicated capacity of 200 A100-equivalent GPUs (mix of q4_3 + fp16) with avg utilization ~45%. Monthly GPU spend (cloud + reserved infra amortized) ~ $2.1M. Unit cost (simple) ~ $120 per 1M tokens given current model mix and batching of 12ms per token.

- Growth+: add incremental 40 GPUs/month for 6 months (peaks at ~440 GPUs), utilization holds ~55% with smarter routing and autoscaling. Monthly spend peaks ~ $4.3M. Unit cost improves to ~$95/1M tokens assuming batching improvements.

- Stress: 30% traffic spike for one month requires immediate burst capacity; option A = overprovision (hot spare) +20% GPUs, option B = temporary cloud burst at spot with fallbacks. Burst delta cost for option B (one month) estimated +$900k; option A ongoing cost +$650k/month.

Key sensitivity: batching latency/throughput trade. If we can safely increase batching window to allow 20% more batching, unit costs drop by ~15% across scenarios. Prefix/KV caching of hot prefixes saves roughly 8–12% in token computation for conversational workloads.

I attached a short sim (batching_cache_sim_summary.pdf) with the baseline vs +20% batching scenarios and a tab in the spreadsheet with assumptions. Will refine numbers with Evelyn's model mix inputs.

—Marcus
Senior Director, Serving Platforms
From: Evelyn Hart <evelyn_hart@redwood.ai>
To: Marcus Lin <marcus_lin@redwood.ai>, Karthik Iyer <karthik_iyer@redwood.ai>
Cc: Laura Bennett <laura_bennett@redwood.ai>, Vivek Kulkarni <vivek_kulkarni@redwood.ai>
Date: Mon, 19 Oct 2026 15:05:00 -0700
Subject: Re: Quarterly ops prep: capacity scenarios & unit-cost tradeoffs

Marcus / Karthik —

I added a model-mix sheet and converted GPU-hours to token-equivalents. High-level assumptions (also in unit_econ_assumptions.txt):

- Model mix: 60% Llama-3-like open model (q4_0 / q4_1), 30% mid-size tuned model, 10% large LLM (fp16).
- Quantization: assume we can operate 75% of traffic on q4_0/q4_1 without quality regressions (A/B evals passed).
- KV cache: assume 25% prefix reuse for chat workloads; this reduces recurrent costs for multi-turn sessions by ~20% of token compute.

Numbers: converted to $/1M tokens, baseline = $118, growth+ (with batching + caching) = $92, stress month w/ cloud burst = $165 (for that month only). I added a sensitivity table that shows changes if batching gains are only 10% vs 20%.

Risks: if we misestimate prefix reuse (e.g., drop to 10%), savings shrink significantly and capacity needs increase. Also watch headroom for cold-start latency if we aggressively quantize larger models.

Attached: unit_econ_assumptions.txt, updated capacity_scenarios_v2.xlsx, batching_cache_sim_summary.pdf.

—Evelyn
Director, Applied ML Ops
From: Vivek Kulkarni <vivek_kulkarni@redwood.ai>
To: Karthik Iyer <karthik_iyer@redwood.ai>, Marcus Lin <marcus_lin@redwood.ai>, Evelyn Hart <evelyn_hart@redwood.ai>, Laura Bennett <laura_bennett@redwood.ai>
Date: Tue, 20 Oct 2026 09:42:00 -0700
Subject: Re: Quarterly ops prep: capacity scenarios & unit-cost tradeoffs

Thanks for the quick turnaround. Short executive asks before I present:

1) One-slide summary: choose baseline and growth+ story. Show clearly where batching/caching reduces the need for incremental Dedicated commits.
2) Recommendation: which option do we want to pre-approve for stress month (cloud burst vs hot spare) and what is the trigger? I prefer cloud burst with an automated budget cap, but note any SLA implications.

Operational asks: Laura — risk/lead time note (how quickly can we spin Dedicated capacity and what procurement approvals are required). Marcus — add a small chart showing unit-cost vs utilization (40% -> 70%) with current stack. Evelyn — include a worst-case quality check note for q4 quantization.

I'll fold this into the leadership one-pager and want to share with CRO & CFO before Thursday. Can you get the final packet to me by EOD Wed?

—Vivek
VP, Operations
From: Laura Bennett <laura_bennett@redwood.ai>
To: Vivek Kulkarni <vivek_kulkarni@redwood.ai>, Karthik Iyer <karthik_iyer@redwood.ai>, Marcus Lin <marcus_lin@redwood.ai>, Evelyn Hart <evelyn_hart@redwood.ai>
Date: Tue, 20 Oct 2026 16:28:00 -0700
Subject: Re: Quarterly ops prep: capacity scenarios & unit-cost tradeoffs

Vivek / Team —

Quick on lead times and procurement: Dedicated pool provisioning (typical) = 6–8 weeks from signed quote (includes infra ordering and network config), but we can enable a limited interim Dedicated via partner cloud accounts in ~10 days for smaller increments (up to 50 GPUs) with appropriate billing flags. Procurement approvals needed for >$500k monthly committed spend require VP sign-off + Finance review — that is our gate.

Recommendation: proceed with cloud-burst policy for stress months with a $1M upper cap and automated alerts at 60% of the cap. Concurrently, approve a growth+ phased commit (40 GPUs/month for 6 months) subject to mid-quarter check if utilization falls below 45%.

I'll prepare the risk slide and procurement checklist and attach to the packet.

—Laura
Director, Cloud Partnerships & Procurement
